 Ranking Member Angie Craig Slams Trump Administration Effort to Kick an Additional 6.3 Million Americans off SNAP
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 Print this Page 
 Share by Email 
 Washington, 
 November 9, 2026 
 | 
 Britton T. Burdick 
 Tags: 
 Nutrition and Foreign Agriculture 
 , 
 Full Committee 
 Today, House Agriculture Committee Ranking Member Angie Craig (MN-02) released the following statement in response to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s proposed rule to eliminate broad-based categorical eligibility (BBCE). BBCE gives states the option to allow someone who has already qualified for Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) or similar state benefits to qualify for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), since their eligibility requirements are similar.
 “This move by the Trump administration to take food assistance away from millions more elderly Americans and children is heartless and cruel,” said Ranking Member Craig . “The proposed rule would make it harder to meet basic needs and roll back efforts to streamline federal programs. SNAP is a highly effective and efficient program when it is allowed to work as designed. Unfortunately, the Trump administration and the outgoing Republican majority in Congress have undermined the program’s integrity at every turn, harming millions of vulnerable Americans in the process. If Congressional Republicans want to be responsive to the needs of American citizens, they can start by joining Democrats in loud and unified opposition to the Trump administration’s latest attack on hungry Americans.”
 According to the Trump administration’s regulatory impact analysis of the proposed rule:
 6.3 million individuals in 3.2 million households will lose their SNAP benefits entirely.
 The 3.2 million families impacted make up 17 percent of SNAP households.
 SNAP benefits will be cut by $50.82 billion. 
 Federal spending on benefits will be cut by $44.65 billion over 5 years (FY2027-FY2031), and state spending on benefits will be cut by $6.17 billion.
 SNAP administrative expenses will increase by $1.24 billion. 
 Federal spending on administrative expenses will increase by $309.5 million over five years.
 State spending on administrative costs will increase by $928.5 million.
 Increased burden on participants is estimated to be approximately $71.7 million over five years.
 Because SNAP participation is often used to streamline eligibility for basic needs programs, the proposed rule's effects reach beyond the program.
 1.78 million children would no longer be categorically eligible for school meals. Of those children: 
 97 percent would likely remain eligible but need to go through an onerous paperwork process to maintain eligibility.
 93,000 children would be shifted from free to reduced-price school meals.
 28,000 children would lose free school meals entirely and have to pay full price.
 42,000 children will no longer receive Summer EBT (“Sun Bucks”) beginning in the summer of 2029. 
 An estimated 13,000 of these children would lose benefits they qualify for due to administrative burden (i.e., not applying for SEBT, even though they remain eligible).
 5,500 women, infants and children would be kicked off the Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants and Children (WIC).
 The number of states opting in to broad-based categorical eligibility has increased steadily each year because of its positive impacts on participants and program administration. Currently, 46 states, Republican and Democratic alike, opt to use BBCE.
 Since the implementation of Trump’s so-called One Big Beautiful Bill, an estimated 5.5 million Americans have already been kicked off SNAP , including around 2 million children.
